Evaluate biomarker recovery from a saliency map

Source: R/evaluate_simulation.R
evaluate_biomarker_recovery.Rd

Two complementary metrics on the same saliency map and ground-truth biomarker spec:

Usage

evaluate_biomarker_recovery(
  saliency_map,
  biomarkers,
  H = NULL,
  W = NULL,
  match_radius_rt = 8L,
  match_radius_cv = 2L,
  top_k = 10L
)

Arguments

saliency_map

numeric H x W matrix in the same coordinate frame as the biomarker locations (i.e. after any padding / trimming used for the encoder input).

biomarkers

ground-truth spec: tibble with at least rt_loc and cv_loc columns (as fractions of image dimensions).

H, W

dimensions of saliency_map. If NULL, taken from the matrix.

match_radius_rt, match_radius_cv

match radius in pixels. Default 8 RT / 2 CV, matching the peak-detector's default min_sep_rt, min_sep_cv.

top_k

number of local maxima to extract for precision/recall.

Value

list(auc_per_pixel, precision_at_k, recall_at_k, matched_biomarkers, missed_biomarkers, top_hotspots)

Details

  1. Per-pixel AUC: label each pixel 1 if within (match_radius_rt, match_radius_cv) of any biomarker center, else 0; score with the saliency value; report ROC AUC. This is "does saliency track biomarker regions on average?"

  2. Top-K precision / recall: extract the top-K non-max-suppressed local maxima of the saliency map; for each, check whether it falls within the match radius of any biomarker center. Precision = matched / K. Recall = unique biomarkers matched / n_biomarkers. This is "does saliency's hotspot list correspond to the biomarkers?"
